text: Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.

(who had already been convicted under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code in a separate set of proceedings) and a number of other persons, starting from 20 February 2008, carried out organisational activities for the purpose of creating discontent in society towards the conduct and results of the election and preparing the crowd gathered at Freedom Square for use of violence and disobedience.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and others spread false information about the assembly being authorised by the authorities, about around 500,000 people attending it, about the election result being rigged, and about presidential candidate Levon Ter-Petrosyan winning about 60% of the votes cast.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and others provided demonstrators at Freedom Square with household items and money to ensure their constant presence at the assembly.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that rods, clubs, armature, petrol bombs, metal constructions used as missile weapons, firearms and ammunition were distributed to a group of participants of the assembly at Freedom Square.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that with the intention of inciting and carrying out mass disorder in Yerevan on 1 March 2008, the members of the group formed groups of people ready to use violence on a mass scale and organised distribution among those persons of illegally obtained firearms, ammunition, explosive substances, explosive devices, bladed weapons and various objects adapted to inflict violence.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan held that, having found out about the imminent arrival of the police forces in the early morning of 1 March 2008, the applicant, together with his co-thinkers, woke up those camping at Freedom Square and called on them to arm themselves and to give a 'proper welcome' to the police.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan held that as a result of the applicant's actions, the crowd attacked the police officers who had approached and asked to carry out an inspection for weapons.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan held that the police operation at Freedom Square eventually led to the discovery of various weapons and ammunition, which had been brought to Freedom Square to be used during the planned mass disorder.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the participants of the assembly, led by the applicant, A.A. and others, moved to and gathered in the area adjacent to the Myasnikyan monument, an important intersection of several streets in Yerevan situated in the vicinity of the French, Italian and Russian embassies.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that at around 11 a.m. on 1 March 2008 the participants of the mass disorder blocked Grigor Lusavorich Street by placing trolleybuses across the driveway, after which they attacked the police officers who were preserving public order.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant, together with A.A., S.M. and others, rejected the offer made by the authorities to move the assembly to another location for the purpose of preserving public order and ensuring the safety of participants.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant, with his speeches and orders, organised and oversaw keeping the gathered crowd in the same location for as long as possible and derailing its relocation, as well as the process of arming themselves with objects adapted to inflict injuries and other objects at hand, assaulting the police officers and showing active disobedience to their lawful orders.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that, as organised and directly instructed by the applicant, S.S. and others, barricades were created by damaging transportation means and other property and by putting them out of order.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant gave instructions to the demonstrators to arm themselves and to be ready to resist, as well as to recruit new people at any cost.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant continuously circulated among the participants in the mass disorder and organised the formation and dislocation of their groups.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant gave concrete instructions to participants to split into groups, build barricades, arm themselves with stones, sticks and other objects in order to injure the police officers, and grab batons and shields from the police officers.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant publicly encouraged the participants in the mass disorder to grab shields and batons from the police officers.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant called on soldiers and police officers involved in maintaining public order not to carry out their duties, to join the participants in the mass disorder and to turn their weapons towards the authorities.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant gave concrete instructions on how to reinforce positions and to prepare for new acts of violence.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant made public declarations about areas captured by the participants in the disorder and declared that all the soldiers had fled and the entire process was under their control, in order to keep the participants in the mass disorder around and to inspire them.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant regularly invited other organisers of the mass disorder for consultations in order to organise and coordinate the activities of its participants.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant regularly exchanged information with A.A. and S.S. about the massacre, arson, intentional destruction, damage and looting of property taking place on Grigor Lusavorich, Mashtots, Leo and Paronyan streets of Yerevan.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan concluded that the events in question amounted to 'mass disorder' within the meaning of Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

section_path: I. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Ad Hoc Public Report of Armenia's Human Rights Defender (Ombudsman): On the 2008 February 19 Presidential Election and the Post-Electoral Developments

text: In its Resolutions regarding the 19 February 2008 presidential election and the events that followed, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe condemned the arrest and continuing detention of scores of persons, including more than 100 opposition supporters and three members of parliament.

The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe condemned the arrest and continuing detention of opposition supporters and members of parliament on seemingly artificial and politically motivated charges, especially those under Articles 225 and 300 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

Relevant extracts of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe Resolutions and a number of other relevant international materials regarding the 19 February 2008 presidential election and post-election events can be found in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia (no. 23086/08, §§ 125-34, 20 September 2018) and Myasnik Malkhasyan v. Armenia (no. 49020/08, §§ 50-57, 15 October 2020).
